declarative.why: names the values a query screen sends its named query: each is an expression over $user, sent as ?name=value

notLower.why: the browser has no other way to fill a query's $params; a flow cannot parameterise a screen's own data source

twice.note: ONE APP ONLY: ride-hailing `my-driver-rides` (query RidesOfDriver, params {account: $user.id}), added 2026-11-18. Before that the client validated `params` and never sent them; core.js listQuery now does.

enforced.note: ride-hailing's drive_s2.py experience stage asserts the screen's dataUrl/params from /api/x/me and that RidesOfDriver?account=driver1 lists driver1's ride while driver2 asking for account=driver1 gets none (row access still applies); experience-client.test.mjs covers listQuery's params. Not browser-driven.

taught.bundleLine: `query` + `params` (a named query instead of `concept`; `"params":{"account":"$user.id"}` fills the query's `$params.account`)
